properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a FIRST-PASS REVIEW OF openmbee.org — the website, the GitHub org listing and one (truncated) architecture page. Nothing here rests on reading their source or running it. Anthony intends to clone the repo for a deep review, and every reading below should be re-tested then. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's stated purpose is 'an open source collaborative engineering system' that 'enables engineers to work in the language of their choice and easily share and document their work across other tools', with the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere'. Its answer to multi-organisation, multi-tool work is LINKED DATA — an RDF quadstore where the fourth term is a named graph, so many contexts coexist in one repository, plus transclusion so one source of truth appears in many places. WHY THIS IS THE AREA WHERE THEY ARE PLAINLY AHEAD OF reflow2, and it is not a small one: it is precisely the operating context Anthony described — several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs that must be made to interoperate although they were never designed to. reflow2 has `req:design-composes`, `compose_and_analyse`, `pair_designs` and `mirror_surface`, and `dec:linked-repos-poc` has sat PARKED since it was filed. Those compose EXPORTS — whole documents, pairwise — where OpenMBEE federates a live graph across repositories. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is strong: reflow2 already decided against the architecture that makes their approach possible. `dec:repo-file-embedded` (the graph lives as a repo file, embedded, not a service) and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service) are the opposite answer to the same question, taken deliberately. A quadstore federation is a service, and adopting the capability may mean reopening those. NOTE ALSO that `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` are BOTH still proposed in this design — OpenMBEE is a fairly complete picture of what saying yes to them costs and buys, which makes it evidence for those two questions whether or not this one is ever answered. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether federation can be had at the EXPORT seam — `export_surface` and `mirror_surface` already publish a subset — rather than requiring a live shared store.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 federate heterogeneous designs across organisations the way OpenMBEE does, rather than composing exports?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill because this is an idea from a landscape review, not intent Anthony has stated. He asked for the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger to be captured as proposed ideas ahead of a deep review, in those words. DELIBERATELY LEFT UNLINKED: `describe_schema {from: Decision, to: Decision}` reports that NO edge type models the pair and that the seventeen which validate do so only through a `*` wildcard — 'validating is not the same as meaning what you intend… prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong'. So this will surface as an `orphan_node` info finding, exactly as `dec:linked-repos-poc` does, and that is the true description of a parked idea rather than a defect to route around.
